title: Thousands of Corals Spawn Together, Timed by the Full Moon

scenes.text: Thousands of corals spawn on the same night.
On the Great Barrier Reef, they release eggs and sperm bundles together.
It happens a few nights after a late spring full moon.
Sunset, the moon cycle and sea temperature all help line up the timing.
When scientists first recorded it in 1981, 32 species spawned together.
The water fills with eggs, like a snowstorm in reverse. Thousands of corals, one night.

description:
Thousands of corals on the Great Barrier Reef spawn together on a few nights each year.
It happens after a late spring full moon, and the first scientists to record it in 1981 saw 32 species release eggs and sperm at once.
Would you dive on spawning night?
thumbnail_text: REEF SPAWNS ON THE SAME NIGHT
first_comment: Fun fact: the moon helps set the timing. Would you dive at night to see it?
